pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Carshalton CofE Primary School - Christian Vision and Values
pageCache.text:
Working in partnership with:
Christian Vision and Values
Christian Vision
Our vision at All Saints is 'For each one of us to shine as a light believing we can make a difference in this world.' Matthew 5:16.
Through our Christian ethos, we learn how we can each shine in our own special way and how we can make a difference in a positive way. We aim to spread positivity and become excellent role models both inside of school and outside when we leave.
Christian Values
At All Saints, we believe that if children display these values inside and outside of school, this will stand them in good stead for whichever path they choose after leaving us. We teach these nine values through worship, class activities, lessons, Bible stories, quotes and inspirational heroes. Our children learn how to show these values and we look for ambassadors who display these values throughout the school day. One child in every class is selected to become an ambassador for each of these values over the school year and they are presented with a special badge which they can wear on their uniform to show how proud we are of each and every child.
Mission and Aims
All Saints School aims to provide a high standard of education within a Christian community where every person is valued as an individual.

Faith Group
At All Saints, our Faith Group includes children from Years 1-6 who were voted for by members of their class. We meet regularly each week to meet, discuss and take part in special projects to improve the spirituality of our school, alongside practising for our Collective Worship and regularly changing our value display. Each lunch time, we open our special reflective area to invite children and staff to take part in reflective activities that are linked to our value and offer opportunities to write prayers.
•To help everyone in school to flourish and shine their light.
•To help us all learn about God’s values.
•To create and look after our reflective spaces around school.
•To follow Jesus’s example and serve others.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Carshalton CofE Primary School - Welcome
pageCache.text:
Working in partnership with:
Welcome from the Head Teacher
For each one of us to shine with God's light, believing we can make a difference in His world.
Welcome to All Saints Carshalton, Church of England Primary School.
Since 1969, All Saints has been at the heart of the community and we continue to be a happy and high achieving school to this day.
Our children learn in an exciting and stimulating environment where all staff members are committed to the highest standards of teaching and learning. We expect these high expectations to be reflected in our pupils and parents and this allows each and every child to reach for and obtain the highest achievements possible, within a safe and Christian environment.
Our ethos is rooted in our nine Christian values: Faith, Love, Hope, Forgiveness, Trust, Friendship, Respect, Peace and Courage. These values, which are shown consistently by staff and children, support us to develop as individuals, becoming more confident and allowing us to celebrate our successes. We show mutual respect and a love of learning in all we do.
Every child is different and has their own talents and skills which we build on in order to prepare them for whatever the future holds, without limits. We value the strong partnership we have with parents and know that with their support our children will develop with confidence, security and success.
We look forward to working in partnership with you and invite you to look at our website to find out more information about our thriving school.
Mrs Laurielle Jackson

Satellites Club
A Breakfast and After School Club now run on site at All Saints Carshalton, Church of England Primary School.
Please click here to download the leaflet.
playsafeadmin@jancett.co.uk
https://jancettplaysafe.co.uk/
About us
Satellites Breakfast and After School Clubs is now run on site at All Saints Carshalton.
Satellites Breakfast Club is open from 7.30am until the gates open at 8.45am
Satellites After School Club is open from end of school to 6.15pm Monday to Friday (excluding bank holidays).
Our Holiday Club runs from 7.45am to 6.30pm during holiday times at
Holmwood Gardens Holiday Club
Admin Tel: 020 8669 1725
https://jancettplaysafe.co.uk/holiday-clubs/
Routine
The Satellites club leaders will meet and greet the children at a designated area in the school playground. The children are given their tea first and then invited to play throughout the rest of the session. Our club provides varied and challenging activities, indoors and outdoors, ensuring that all play opportunities are offered at each session.
Each child can choose what they like to do and join in the activities, which at all times adhere to both equal opportunities and health and safety.
Activities can include: dance and drama, face painting, games and puzzles, homework, quiet corner, science, cooking, creative writing, messy play, quizzes and arts and crafts.
What Ofsted say about Satellites
Children arrive confidently and are settled in the club. Their happiness at being in the club is evident as they link up with friends and very enthusiastically make their way to the good range of resources. The children confidently approach staff indicating good and trusting relationships are built.

Extra Curricular
Clubs play an important role within the school community.
They contribute to the development of relationships, both child/child and child/adult. They encourage the expectation in a child of actively using leisure time and also provide additional opportunities for success.
Children also have the opportunity to take part in numerous clubs, which take place before, during lunchtime and after school. (See current clubs timetable below).
Clubs do not run in the first or last week of term.
Morning clubs start at 8.15am. Please bring your child to the school office and wait with them until an adult has taken them into school.
Afterschool clubs finish at 4.30pm. Children will come straight from class to their club, you collect from the school office at 4.30pm.
Booking is not required for lunchtime clubs (with the exception of Songbirds & Crochet/Knitting Club due to capacity), please just turn up at the allotted time and location.
There is a small charge for clubs. £1 for morning clubs per child per session. £2 for afternoon clubs per child per session.
Clubs run by external providers please contact them directly for full details.

Music
Music is taught in all classes and follows the National Curriculum guidelines.
Children are given frequent opportunities to sing, listen to and develop an understanding of a wide range of music from different times and places, and to present ideas through their own compositions, which can be performed to others.
They enjoy composing and performing using a huge variety of instruments, which include tuned and untuned percussion, xylophones and glockenspiels, keyboard, recorder and ukulele. We have both Extra Curricular music at the school includes the Infant (Songbirds) and Junior (Rockin' Robins) Choirs and Orchestra, which perform for the school and the local community during the year. In addition, children in Year 3 learn to play the recorder and in Year 5 and 6 the ukulele. There are also opportunities for junior children to learn to play a variety of musical instruments including: guitar, flute, clarinet, saxophone, brass and strings.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Carshalton CofE Primary School - E-Safety
pageCache.text:
Working in partnership with:
E-Safety at All Saints
Online safety plays an important role in keeping our children safe, both at school and at home. Online safety is taught to all pupils and will be covered within the Computing curriculum. Talking to children about what they are doing online is a fantastic way to understand the internet further.
Throughout the school, an emphasis is put on using technology safely, ensuring all our pupils know where to go should they have any concerns. We will also provide the children with the ability to recognise when something isn’t quite right in the first place. The E-cadets also play an important role in school, helping to promote the significance of online safety, as well as being a trusted person the children can turn to.
Computing is at the heart of our learning as we prepare the children for the future. We encourage you to take the opportunity to engage with your child to understand more about the internet too. As a parent or carer, it is your responsibility to make sure you are aware of what your child is using the internet for and that it is age-appropriate.

pageCache.pageTitle: All Saints Carshalton CofE Primary School - School Meals and Menu
pageCache.text:
Working in partnership with:
School Meals and Menu
All children from Reception to Year 6 are welcome to have a school lunch here at All Saints Carshalton.
We're thrilled to announce that this term, our children have taken the reins in selecting their favourite meals for our school menu. Through a collaborative effort, each class has voted for new and exciting dishes to tickle their taste buds, and the School Council has skillfully put together everyone's ideas into a selection of six delicious meals to enjoy between now and the end of the school year. Mrs Bramble has ensured that the children's suggestions comply with school food guidelines.
This initiative not only empowers our children by allowing them to play a pivotal role in shaping their dining experience but also fosters a sense of community and cooperation within our school.
Autumn Term Menu 2026
For the academic year 2023/2024 children in Year 3,4,5 and 6 will also receive a Free School meal. This is an initiative started by the Mayor of London, which is currently only in place for 1 academic year.
Children are also very welcome to have a packed lunch brought in from home. We ask please that these are healthy and filling. We also ask that they do not contain any nuts, sweets, chocolate or juice. Children will be provided with water to have alongside their lunches.
Please have a look at the below link for some healthy option ideas for packed lunches;
https://www.nhs.uk/healthier-families/recipes/healthier-lunchboxes/
*If you think that you may be entitled to means test Free School Meals you can check your eligibility by following this link the the local authority's website;
https://www.sutton.gov.uk/w/apply-for-free-school-meals-1?p_l_back_url=%2Fsearch%3Fq%3DFree%2Bschool%2Bmeals
